properties.exception_pathway: A team requesting a deviation from the log-schema or retention requirements submits a request via the shared policy exception register (per the Engineering Policy Governance Policy's mechanism); the SRE Lead accountable for the affected service reviews and time-boxes any grant, capped at 90 days, with a written risk-acceptance rationale.
properties.measurable_outcomes: 100% of production services have logs conforming to the log-schema standard; zero retention-integrity check failures left unescalated past their 1-business-day SLA in a given quarter.
properties.capability_grouping_rationale: Governs only cap-10 (Security Logging). This Policy is deliberately kept separate from Slice 7's upcoming Data Protection and Privacy Engineering Policy (governing cap-9), applying AC-BI-010's genuinely-different-ownership-model test: the two have different accountable owners (SRE Lead here vs. the Data Protection Officer there) and fundamentally different control models -- this Policy's controls are CI/scheduled-job automatable mechanical checks (log-schema validation, retention-integrity verification) that run continuously with no human judgment call, whereas privacy-by-design review is a human-led design review assessing proportionality and legal basis before a feature ships. Merging them would make one owner accountable for a control model they don't run, and would obscure that a log spilling raw personal data is a *different* failure from a log simply expiring early -- both real, but caught by different mechanisms. One Policy (not two) suffices here because only one Capability, cap-10, falls in this slice's scope: SRE Lead owns both the log-schema half and the retention-integrity half under one integrated control model, mirroring Slice 5's single-Policy pattern where a further split would have been reflexive, not warranted.

properties.title: Structured Security Log Schema Standard
properties.description: Defines the required structured log schema and field set for access and security logs emitted by production services.
properties.procedure: 1) Every production service must emit access and security log events in the organization's structured log schema (JSON, with a defined field set: timestamp, actor identity, action, resource, outcome, source origin). 2) The Security Engineer maintains the canonical schema definition and versions it. 3) New services onboard by validating their log output against the current schema version in CI before first production deployment. 4) Any schema change is reviewed jointly by the SRE Lead and Security Engineer, and a migration window is set for existing services.
properties.applicability_boundary: Applies to all production services' access and security log output; does not apply to debug/trace-level application logs with no security or access relevance.
properties.verification_notes: A Control can test conformance by validating a sample of each service's emitted log events against the current schema definition in CI: (a) required fields present, (b) field types match, (c) no unstructured free-text line substituted for a required structured event.
properties.change_rationale: Newly authored as the first Standard under the Data Handling, Logging, and Audit Retention Policy; no predecessor version exists.

properties.title: Security Log Retention and Integrity Standard
properties.description: Defines the retention period and integrity-verification procedure for access and security logs, so they remain available and unaltered for the duration needed to support traceability and audit evidence.
properties.procedure: 1) Access and security logs are retained for a minimum of 400 days, aligned to the organization's audit-evidence window, in write-once storage. 2) A scheduled job computes and records a retention-integrity check daily, confirming for each service that its expected log volume for the prior day is present and no log segment within the retention window has been deleted or altered outside the log pipeline's own append path. 3) Any detected gap or integrity failure is escalated to the SRE Lead within 1 business day and tracked as an incident until remediated. 4) Logs reaching the end of the retention window are purged per the organization's data-retention schedule and the purge is recorded in the purge log.
properties.applicability_boundary: Applies to all structured access and security logs in scope of the Structured Security Log Schema Standard; does not apply to ephemeral debug logs outside that scope.
properties.verification_notes: A Control can test conformance by checking: (a) every service's expected log volume for each day in the retention window is present, (b) the daily retention-integrity check ran and recorded a result, (c) no integrity failure remained unescalated past 1 business day, (d) no log segment was purged before its retention window elapsed.
properties.change_rationale: Newly authored as the second Standard under the Data Handling, Logging, and Audit Retention Policy; no predecessor version exists.

properties.title: CI Structured Access Log Schema Validator
properties.description: Automated CI check that validates each service's emitted log samples against the current structured log schema before deployment.
properties.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if 100% of validated log samples for the build contain all required schema fields with correct types and no unstructured line substituted for a required event. FAIL if any required field is missing, mistyped, or a required event is emitted as unstructured free text.
properties.execution_method: Runs automatically on every CI build as a pre-deployment gate, evaluating a captured sample of the service's log output against the current schema version; intended to run on every build once wired in.
properties.evidence_plan: Per-build validation results (pass/fail, field-level diff on failure) will be written to the CI build log and referenced by build ID in the engineering compliance evidence store.
properties.risk_alignment_rationale: Directly verifies s6-rp-1 (Traceability and Auditability): a log stream missing required fields or emitted as unstructured text is exactly the untraceable-evidence failure mode that risk path describes -- an incident investigator or auditor unable to reconstruct who did what, when.

properties.title: Automated Security Log Retention Integrity Check
properties.description: Automated scheduled job that verifies, for every in-scope service, that the expected log volume for the prior day is present in write-once storage and no log segment within the retention window has been deleted or altered outside the pipeline's append path.
properties.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if every in-scope service's expected log volume for the checked day is present and no unauthorized modification or deletion is detected anywhere in the current retention window. FAIL if any service's expected log volume is missing, or any out-of-band modification or deletion is detected.
properties.execution_method: Scheduled job runs daily against the log storage's integrity metadata (checksums / append-only ledger); intended cadence: daily, once scheduled.
properties.evidence_plan: Daily per-service integrity check results will be written to the engineering compliance evidence store as a dated report, referenced by service and date.
properties.risk_alignment_rationale: Directly verifies s6-rp-1: a gap or silent alteration in retained logs is exactly the undetected-evidence-loss failure mode that risk path describes -- retention that exists as policy text but not as a verified fact.

properties.title: Quarterly Audit Evidence Sampling Review
properties.description: Manual quarterly review where the Security Engineer samples retained access/security logs across a cross-section of services and confirms they are complete, schema-conformant, and sufficient to reconstruct a representative access event end-to-end.
properties.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if every sampled service's logs allow the reviewer to fully reconstruct at least one representative access event end-to-end with no missing or unreadable segment. FAIL if any sampled service's logs are incomplete, unreadable, or insufficient to reconstruct a representative event.
properties.execution_method: Manual review performed quarterly by the Security Engineer, sampling a rotating cross-section of production services and their retained logs. Intended cadence: quarterly, calendar-aligned.
properties.evidence_plan: Review findings (per sampled service, pass/fail and any gap identified) will be recorded in the audit-evidence review log as a dated entry per service per quarter.
properties.risk_alignment_rationale: Directly verifies s6-rp-1 by testing the end-to-end auditability claim the automated checks (s6-ctrl-1/s6-ctrl-2) can't fully cover on their own -- proving logs are not just present and unaltered, but actually usable to answer a real audit or incident question.

properties.title: Log Retention Window Purge Compliance Check
properties.description: Automated check verifying that no log segment was purged before its retention window elapsed, and that every purge past the window was recorded in the purge log.
properties.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if every purge event in the evaluation window occurred at or after the log segment's full retention period and is recorded in the purge log. FAIL if any log segment was purged before its retention window elapsed, or any purge event has no corresponding purge-log record.
properties.execution_method: Scheduled job cross-checks the storage system's deletion events against the purge log and each segment's retention-window start date; intended cadence: daily, once scheduled.
properties.evidence_plan: Purge-compliance check results will be written to the engineering compliance evidence store as a dated report, referenced by service and purge event ID.
properties.risk_alignment_rationale: Directly verifies s6-rp-1: evidence purged early -- whether accidental or malicious -- is a direct loss of the traceability and audit evidence this risk path exists to protect; this Control is the concrete mechanism that catches that failure mode before it becomes an unrecoverable audit gap.

properties.name: Traceability and Auditability
properties.description: Risk that engineering systems cannot reconstruct who did what, when, or cannot produce log evidence sufficient to support an audit or incident investigation -- because access/security logs are not structured consistently, are lost or silently altered before their required retention period elapses, or are purged early -- resulting in an unresolvable incident investigation, a failed compliance audit, or an inability to demonstrate accountability after the fact.

properties.name: Data Protection and Privacy Engineering
properties.description: Practice area covering privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default engineering practices, personal-data minimization in default configurations, and the technical and organizational safeguards needed to protect personal data proportionate to its sensitivity and legal basis.

properties.title: Data Protection and Privacy Engineering Policy
properties.description: Establishes mandatory privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default engineering practices, requiring personal-data minimization by default and proportionate technical and organizational safeguards across the software development lifecycle.
properties.scope_in: All internally developed services and features that collect, process, or store personal data, including privacy-by-design review at design time, personal-data minimization in default configurations, and proportionate technical/organizational safeguards (encryption, pseudonymization, access restriction) matched to data sensitivity and legal basis.
properties.scope_out: Any specific external data-protection regulation's own Articles or Policy/Standard/Control content -- this Policy System's Domain Mapper never authors Policy/Standard/Control for an external source (ps-domain-concepts.md:43-44), so there is no external Policy of this kind to defer to or duplicate; general access-control/authentication mechanics for engineering tooling, governed separately by the Access Control Policy (s2-pol-2); log retention/audit-evidence mechanics, governed separately by the Data Handling, Logging, and Audit Retention Policy (s6-pol-1).
properties.normative_commitments: Every feature or service that collects or processes personal data must complete a privacy-by-design review before its first production release and after any material change to what personal data is collected or how it is used. Default system and process configurations must minimize personal-data collection, exposure, and retention; no feature may ship with a default that widens personal-data collection or retention without a recorded proportionality justification. Technical and organizational safeguards applied to personal data must be proportionate to that data's sensitivity and the legal basis for processing it.
properties.review_cadence: Reviewed every 12 months, and immediately upon any material change to the organization's data-protection legal-basis inventory or privacy-review tooling.
properties.exception_pathway: A team requesting an exception from a privacy-by-design finding or a default-minimization requirement submits it via the shared policy exception register (per the Engineering Policy Governance Policy's mechanism); the Data Protection Officer accountable for the affected processing activity reviews and time-boxes any grant, capped at 90 days, with a written risk-acceptance rationale naming the specific proportionality gap.
properties.measurable_outcomes: 100% of features that collect or process personal data have a completed, DPO-approved privacy-by-design review before first production release; zero default configurations found, on quarterly sampling, to collect or retain personal data beyond what the recorded legal basis and proportionality justification support.
properties.capability_grouping_rationale: Governs only cap-9 (renamed this slice from 'Data Protection by Design & Default' to 'Privacy by Design and Default' to converge onto GDPR-1.0's existing Capability of that exact name, id cap_privacy_by_design_and_default_fbdf54 -- GDPR's own description, 'A process for embedding data protection measures into systems and operations from the outset and ensuring only necessary personal data is processed by default settings,' covers both the design-time and default-configuration halves of cap-9's original scope, unlike GDPR's narrower 'Data Protection by Default' Capability (cap_data_protection_by_default_0e4e38, 'Default system and process settings are configured to minimize data exposure...'), which omits the by-design half entirely -- so 'Privacy by Design and Default' is the closer real-world match and was used for the rename. Unlike every other Policy authored so far in this dataset, this is the FIRST Policy governing a Capability with no possible external Policy/Standard/Control to converge onto: ps-domain-concepts.md:43-44 confirms an external RegulatoryInstrument's Domain Mapper stage never reaches Policy/Standard/Control, so GDPR-1.0's own ingestion stopped at Capability and minted no Policy for cap-9 to converge onto (unlike, e.g., cap-5's Policy converging onto CRA's pre-existing SBOM Capability naming). This Policy is therefore scored on its own merits as a fresh internal authoring, not against a nonexistent 'existing Policy' comparison. Its ownership (Data Protection Officer) and control model (privacy-by-design design review plus default-configuration minimization and retention checks) are genuinely distinct from every other Policy in this dataset, including the logging/retention-focused Data Handling, Logging, and Audit Retention Policy (s6-pol-1), which already scoped this exact split out in its own capability_grouping_rationale.

properties.title: Privacy-by-Design Review Standard
properties.description: Defines the procedure for conducting a privacy-by-design review before a feature or service that processes personal data reaches production.
properties.procedure: 1) Before first production release, or after any material change to what personal data is collected or how it is used, the owning team completes a privacy-by-design review documenting: data flows, categories of personal data involved, legal basis for processing, and proportionality of the safeguards applied. 2) The Data Protection Officer reviews the documented review and either approves it, requests changes, or records mitigations as backlog items. 3) A feature must not reach production until its privacy-by-design review is DPO-approved. 4) The review is re-conducted after any material architecture change that alters what personal data is collected, how it is processed, or its legal basis.
properties.applicability_boundary: Applies to all internally developed features and services that collect, process, or store personal data prior to first production release and after material changes to that processing; does not apply to features that process no personal data whatsoever.
properties.verification_notes: A Control can test conformance by checking that: (a) every production feature/service that processes personal data has a privacy-by-design review document dated within the last 12 months or since its last material change to personal-data processing, whichever is more recent, (b) the document carries a recorded DPO approval sign-off predating the feature's production release date.
properties.change_rationale: Newly authored as the first Standard under the Data Protection and Privacy Engineering Policy; no predecessor version exists.

properties.title: Default Data Minimization Standard
properties.description: Defines the procedure for verifying that default system and process configurations minimize personal-data collection, exposure, and retention.
properties.procedure: 1) For every feature that collects personal data, the default configuration (behavior with no user or administrator action taken) must collect only the personal-data fields necessary for the feature's stated purpose. 2) Any configuration option that would widen personal-data collection, exposure, or retention beyond the default must require an explicit, auditable opt-in action; it must never ship as the default. 3) The owning team records, in the feature's privacy-by-design review, the specific minimality justification for each personal-data field collected by default. 4) Default retention periods for personal data must be set to the shortest period that satisfies the recorded legal basis and business purpose, and must be reviewed whenever that basis or purpose changes.
properties.applicability_boundary: Applies to all default (out-of-the-box, no user/administrator action taken) configurations of internally developed features that collect or process personal data; does not apply to explicit, auditable opt-in configurations a user or administrator deliberately selects.
properties.verification_notes: A Control can test conformance by sampling shipped default configurations for in-scope features and checking: (a) each personal-data field collected by default has a recorded minimality justification in the feature's privacy-by-design review, (b) no personal-data-widening option is enabled by default, (c) default retention periods match the shortest period the recorded legal basis/purpose supports.
properties.change_rationale: Newly authored as the second Standard under the Data Protection and Privacy Engineering Policy; no predecessor version exists.

properties.title: Privacy-by-Design Review Completion Check
properties.description: Manual verification that every production feature/service processing personal data has a current, DPO-approved privacy-by-design review.
properties.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if every in-scope production feature/service has a privacy-by-design review document dated within the last 12 months (or since its last material change to personal-data processing, whichever is more recent) with a recorded DPO approval sign-off predating its production release date. FAIL if any in-scope feature/service's review is missing, stale, or lacks a DPO sign-off.
properties.execution_method: Manual review performed by the Data Protection Officer against the feature/service inventory, cross-checked against the personal-data-processing change log; intended cadence: quarterly.
properties.evidence_plan: Review results (feature/service name, review date, DPO sign-off status) will be recorded in the engineering compliance evidence store as a dated quarterly report.
properties.risk_alignment_rationale: Directly verifies s7-rp-1 (Data Protection and Privacy): a missing or stale privacy-by-design review is exactly the undetected-personal-data-exposure blind spot that risk path describes -- a feature reaching production without anyone having assessed what personal data it touches or whether its safeguards are proportionate.

properties.title: Automated Default Data Minimization Scan
properties.description: Automated scan of a feature's shipped default configuration verifying it collects only the personal-data fields justified in its privacy-by-design review and enables no personal-data-widening option by default.
properties.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if every personal-data field collected by the feature's default configuration matches a field with a recorded minimality justification in its privacy-by-design review, and no personal-data-widening option is enabled by default. FAIL if any unjustified field is collected by default, or any widening option ships enabled.
properties.execution_method: Runs automatically in the CI pipeline against the feature's default configuration manifest and its linked privacy-by-design review record, on every build touching personal-data-handling code paths; intended to run on every such build once wired in.
properties.evidence_plan: Per-build scan results (fields checked, pass/fail, any unjustified field flagged) will be written to the CI build log and referenced by build ID in the engineering compliance evidence store.
properties.risk_alignment_rationale: Directly verifies s7-rp-1: a default configuration that silently collects or exposes more personal data than justified is exactly the proportionality failure this risk path is scoped to catch before it reaches production undetected.

properties.title: Default Retention Period Compliance Check
properties.description: Automated scheduled check verifying personal-data default retention periods match the shortest period their recorded legal basis and purpose support, and that no personal data is retained past its configured period.
properties.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if every in-scope personal-data store's configured retention period matches its recorded legal-basis/purpose justification and no record is found retained past its configured period. FAIL if any store's retention period exceeds its justification, or any record is found past its configured retention period.
properties.execution_method: Scheduled job queries personal-data stores' retention configuration and actual record ages weekly; intended to run every Monday at 06:00 UTC once scheduled.
properties.evidence_plan: Job output (per-store pass/fail, record IDs for any over-retained data) will be written to the engineering compliance evidence store as a dated JSON report, one per run.
properties.risk_alignment_rationale: Directly verifies s7-rp-1: personal data retained beyond what its legal basis and purpose justify is a concrete, checkable instance of the disproportionate-processing exposure this risk path describes, distinct from s7-ctrl-2's design-time default-collection check by catching drift over the data's actual lifetime.

properties.title: Quarterly Proportionality Sampling Review
properties.description: Manual quarterly review where the Data Protection Officer samples a cross-section of production features processing personal data and confirms the safeguards applied remain proportionate to the data's current sensitivity and legal basis.
properties.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if every sampled feature's applied safeguards (encryption, pseudonymization, access restriction) are, in the DPO's documented judgment, proportionate to the personal data's current sensitivity and legal basis. FAIL if any sampled feature's safeguards are found disproportionate -- too weak for the data's current sensitivity, or the legal basis has changed without a corresponding safeguard review.
properties.execution_method: Manual review performed quarterly by the Data Protection Officer, sampling a rotating cross-section of production features that process personal data. Intended cadence: quarterly, calendar-aligned.
properties.evidence_plan: Review findings (per sampled feature, pass/fail and any gap identified) will be recorded in the privacy-review log as a dated entry per feature per quarter.
properties.risk_alignment_rationale: Directly verifies s7-rp-1 by testing the human judgment call the automated checks (s7-ctrl-2/s7-ctrl-3) can't make on their own -- whether the combination of safeguards actually applied remains proportionate as data sensitivity or legal basis shifts over time, not just whether individual fields or retention periods pass a mechanical check.

properties.name: Data Protection and Privacy
properties.description: Risk that personal data is collected, processed, or retained by an engineering system in a way disproportionate to its sensitivity or legal basis -- because privacy-by-design review, default data-minimization, or retention-proportionality controls failed or were bypassed -- resulting in unauthorized exposure, unlawful processing, or an inability to demonstrate proportionate safeguards after the fact.

properties.name: Vulnerability and Incident Management
properties.description: Practice area covering security vulnerability scanning, triage, and severity-based remediation SLAs, together with the incident-response readiness (detection, drills, and postmortems) needed to recover from a security incident once it occurs.

properties.title: Vulnerability Management and Remediation Policy
properties.description: Governs how security vulnerabilities are scanned for, triaged, and remediated within severity-based SLAs, and how the organization detects, responds to, and recovers from a security incident once one occurs.
properties.scope_in: All security vulnerability scanning, triage, and remediation for internally owned services and their dependencies (continuing the build-time scanning already governed by the Secure SDLC Policy into ongoing, post-release vulnerability management); security incident detection, response, escalation, tabletop drills, and postmortem review once a security vulnerability or breach is suspected or confirmed.
properties.scope_out: General service reliability and availability commitments -- Service Level Objective/error-budget tracking, redundancy/failover design, and capacity planning -- which remain governed by the Service Reliability and Availability Policy (s5-pol-1); build-time SAST/dependency/secret scanning gates that block a merge before release, which remain governed by the Secure SDLC Policy (s3-pol-1); this Policy governs what happens to a vulnerability or incident after code has already reached production.
properties.normative_commitments: Every production service and its dependencies must be continuously scanned for known vulnerabilities. Every discovered vulnerability must be triaged and assigned a severity within 2 business days of detection. Remediation (patch, mitigation, or accepted-risk exception) must complete within the SLA for its assigned severity (critical: 7 days, high: 30 days, medium: 90 days). Every suspected security incident must be triaged by an on-call responder within 1 hour, and every confirmed incident must have a completed postmortem within 10 business days of resolution.
properties.review_cadence: Reviewed every 12 months, and immediately upon any material change to the vulnerability-scanning toolchain or the incident-response escalation process.
properties.exception_pathway: A team unable to meet a remediation SLA (e.g. a critical vulnerability with no available patch) submits a request via the shared policy exception register (per the Engineering Policy Governance Policy's mechanism); the Security Engineer accountable for the affected service reviews and time-boxes any grant, capped at 30 days, with a written risk-acceptance rationale and a compensating mitigation.
properties.measurable_outcomes: 100% of discovered vulnerabilities are triaged within 2 business days; at least 95% of remediations complete within their severity's SLA in a given quarter; 100% of confirmed security incidents have a completed postmortem within 10 business days of resolution.
properties.capability_grouping_rationale: Governs only cap-8 (Vulnerability Management), reused unchanged from CRA-1.0's exact-match Capability of that name (confirmed live, id cap_vulnerability_management_da8ef6, description 'Process for receiving, triaging, tracking, and fixing component vulnerabilities, including coordinating remediation actions and status follow-up') -- no rename needed since the stub's existing name already matches exactly. This Policy deliberately absorbs both the vulnerability-management half AND the incident-response half of the guideline's item 10/11 naming (`minimal-engineering-policy-seed-guideline.md` lines 57-58) under one Policy and one owner (Security Engineer), and explicitly does NOT absorb Slice 5's reliability concerns: the Service Reliability and Availability Policy (s5-pol-1) already scoped incident response for SLO/availability breaches out of its own boundary in its own `scope_out` ('Incident detection, triage, and postmortem response once an SLO breach or outage has already occurred, which is governed by the separate Vulnerability Management and Remediation Policy's incident-response half'), explicitly deferring to this Policy by name. That split is deliberate, not reflexive (AC-BI-008/AC-BI-010's minimality test): s5-pol-1 is owned by the SRE Lead with a reliability control model (SLI/SLO monitoring, error-budget gating, failover testing) triggered by a service failing to meet a performance/availability commitment, whereas this Policy is owned by the Security Engineer with a security control model (vulnerability scanning, severity-SLA remediation, incident-response drills and postmortems) triggered by a security exposure or breach -- two genuinely different trigger conditions, owners, and control mechanisms that happen to both use the word 'incident,' not one discipline artificially split by regulation-article boundaries. Keeping them as two Policies avoids making the SRE Lead accountable for a security-incident control model they don't run, and avoids making the Security Engineer accountable for SLO/error-budget mechanics that belong to reliability engineering.

properties.title: Continuous Vulnerability Scanning and Triage Standard
properties.description: Defines the procedure for continuously scanning production services and their dependencies for known vulnerabilities and triaging each finding to an assigned severity.
properties.procedure: 1) Every production service and its runtime dependencies are scanned on a recurring schedule (at minimum daily) for known vulnerabilities using the organization's vulnerability-intelligence feed. 2) Every new finding is triaged by the Security Engineer within 2 business days, assigning a severity (critical/high/medium/low) using the organization's CVSS-aligned severity matrix. 3) Triaged findings are logged in the vulnerability register with the affected service, component, severity, and detection date. 4) A finding already covered by an active, unexpired exception is not re-triaged until the exception expires.
properties.applicability_boundary: Applies to all production services and their direct and transitive runtime dependencies; does not apply to non-production/development environments with no path to production data.
properties.verification_notes: A Control can test conformance by checking: (a) every in-scope service has a scan result dated within the last scan interval, (b) every new finding has a triage record (severity, triage date) within 2 business days of its detection date, (c) no untriaged finding remains open past that window.
properties.change_rationale: Newly authored as the first Standard under the Vulnerability Management and Remediation Policy; no predecessor version exists.

properties.title: Severity-Based Remediation SLA Standard
properties.description: Defines the remediation SLA for each vulnerability severity tier and the escalation path for a remediation at risk of missing its SLA.
properties.procedure: 1) Every triaged vulnerability finding is assigned a remediation deadline based on its severity: critical 7 days, high 30 days, medium 90 days, from triage date. 2) The Security Engineer tracks open findings against their deadlines in the vulnerability register. 3) A finding within 2 days of missing its SLA without a completed remediation or filed exception is automatically escalated to the accountable Engineering Manager. 4) Remediation (patch deployed, mitigation applied, or exception granted per the Policy's exception pathway) closes the finding with a recorded closure date and method.
properties.applicability_boundary: Applies to every vulnerability finding triaged under the Continuous Vulnerability Scanning and Triage Standard; does not apply to findings in decommissioned services with no production traffic.
properties.verification_notes: A Control can test conformance by checking: (a) every closed finding's closure date is at or before its severity's SLA deadline, or is linked to a valid exception record, (b) every finding within 2 days of its deadline with no closure has a logged escalation to the Engineering Manager.
properties.change_rationale: Newly authored as the second Standard under the Vulnerability Management and Remediation Policy; no predecessor version exists.

properties.title: Security Incident Response and Postmortem Standard
properties.description: Defines the procedure for detecting, triaging, and responding to a suspected security incident, and for completing a postmortem once it is resolved.
properties.procedure: 1) A suspected security incident (from monitoring, a vulnerability finding, or an external report) is triaged by the on-call security responder within 1 hour of detection, who declares it confirmed or a false positive. 2) A confirmed incident is assigned an incident commander who coordinates containment, eradication, and recovery, following the incident-response runbook. 3) The Security Engineer schedules an incident-response tabletop drill at least every 6 months, exercising the runbook against a simulated scenario and recording the result. 4) Within 10 business days of a confirmed incident's resolution, the incident commander leads a blameless postmortem documenting root cause, timeline, and follow-up remediation items with owners and target dates.
properties.applicability_boundary: Applies to all suspected or confirmed security incidents affecting production services; does not apply to general service-availability incidents with no suspected security cause, which follow the Service Reliability and Availability Policy's own reliability-review process instead.
properties.verification_notes: A Control can test conformance by checking: (a) every logged suspected incident has an on-call triage record within 1 hour of detection, (b) every confirmed incident has a completed postmortem dated within 10 business days of its resolution date with root cause and follow-up items recorded, (c) a tabletop drill result exists dated within the last 6 months.
properties.change_rationale: Newly authored as the third Standard under the Vulnerability Management and Remediation Policy, covering the incident-response half of the Policy's scope distinct from the scanning/remediation half; no predecessor version exists.

properties.title: Automated Vulnerability Scan Coverage and Triage SLA Check
properties.description: Automated scheduled check verifying every production service has a current vulnerability scan and every new finding was triaged within the 2-business-day SLA.
properties.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if every in-scope service has a scan result dated within the last scan interval and every finding detected in the window has a recorded triage (severity, triage date) within 2 business days of detection. FAIL if any service's scan is stale, or any finding is untriaged past 2 business days.
properties.execution_method: Scheduled job cross-checks the vulnerability register against the scan schedule and each finding's detection/triage timestamps; intended to run daily once scheduled.
properties.evidence_plan: Job output (per-service scan freshness, per-finding triage SLA pass/fail) will be written to the engineering compliance evidence store as a dated daily report.
properties.risk_alignment_rationale: Directly verifies s8-rp-1 (Incident and Recovery Readiness): a service with no current scan, or a finding sitting untriaged, is exactly the undetected/unactioned-vulnerability exposure that lets a fixable weakness silently become an incident.

properties.title: Automated Remediation SLA Compliance Check
properties.description: Automated scheduled check verifying every closed vulnerability finding was remediated within its severity's SLA, or is linked to a valid exception, and that at-risk findings were escalated.
properties.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if every closed finding's closure date is at or before its severity's SLA deadline or is linked to a valid, non-expired exception record, and every finding within 2 days of its deadline with no closure has a logged Engineering Manager escalation. FAIL if any closed finding missed its SLA with no linked exception, or any at-risk finding was not escalated.
properties.execution_method: Scheduled job evaluates the vulnerability register's open and closed findings against their severity-based deadlines; intended to run daily once scheduled.
properties.evidence_plan: Job output (per-finding SLA pass/fail, escalation status) will be written to the engineering compliance evidence store as a dated daily report.
properties.risk_alignment_rationale: Directly verifies s8-rp-1: a vulnerability remediated late, or never escalated when at risk of missing its SLA, is exactly the slow-remediation exposure that lets a known weakness remain exploitable long enough to become an incident.

properties.title: Vulnerability Intelligence Feed Freshness Check
properties.description: Automated check verifying the vulnerability-intelligence feed used for scanning is itself up to date, so scans are evaluated against current known-vulnerability data.
properties.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if the vulnerability-intelligence feed's last successful update is within the defined freshness window (24 hours). FAIL if the feed's last successful update is older than 24 hours, or the last scheduled update failed.
properties.execution_method: Scheduled job checks the feed provider's last-updated timestamp against the scanning toolchain's ingested copy; intended to run every 6 hours once scheduled.
properties.evidence_plan: Feed freshness check results will be written to the engineering compliance evidence store as a dated report, referenced by feed source and check timestamp.
properties.risk_alignment_rationale: Directly verifies s8-rp-1 by grounding the scan-coverage check (s8-ctrl-1) itself: a scan running against stale vulnerability data would report false confidence, silently missing newly disclosed vulnerabilities that could otherwise be caught before becoming an incident.

properties.title: Incident Response Tabletop Drill Verification
properties.description: Manual verification that a security incident-response tabletop drill was conducted within the required 6-month window and that any gap it surfaced was logged with an owner.
properties.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if a tabletop drill result is recorded within the last 6 months, exercising the current incident-response runbook, with any surfaced gap logged with an assigned owner and target date. FAIL if no drill was conducted within the window, or a surfaced gap has no assigned owner/target date.
properties.execution_method: Manual review performed by the Security Engineer against the drill log; intended cadence: every 6 months, aligned to the drill schedule itself.
properties.evidence_plan: Drill results and any logged gaps will be recorded in the incident-response drill log as a dated entry per drill.
properties.risk_alignment_rationale: Directly verifies s8-rp-1's recovery-readiness half: a runbook that has never actually been exercised is exactly the untested-recovery-capability exposure this risk path describes -- an incident-response plan that only looks ready on paper.

properties.title: Post-Incident Postmortem Completion Review
properties.description: Manual review confirming every confirmed security incident has a completed, blameless postmortem within 10 business days of resolution, with root cause and follow-up remediation items recorded.
properties.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if 100% of confirmed security incidents in the review period have a postmortem document dated within 10 business days of resolution, naming a root cause and follow-up items each with an owner and target date. FAIL if any confirmed incident is missing a postmortem, the postmortem is late, or it lacks a root cause or owned follow-up items.
properties.execution_method: Manual review performed by the Engineering Manager sampling the incident log each month; intended cadence: monthly.
properties.evidence_plan: Review results (incident ID, postmortem completeness, pass/fail) will be recorded in the engineering compliance evidence store as a dated monthly report.
properties.risk_alignment_rationale: Directly verifies s8-rp-1 by confirming the organization actually learns from a confirmed incident -- a missing or superficial postmortem is exactly the repeat-failure exposure this risk path is scoped to catch, closing the loop the drill verification (s8-ctrl-4) tests only in simulation.

properties.name: Incident and Recovery Readiness
properties.description: Risk that a security vulnerability or incident goes undetected, untriaged, or unremediated long enough to be exploited, or that when an incident does occur, the organization cannot respond and recover effectively -- because vulnerability scanning coverage or triage SLAs lapsed, remediation missed its severity-based deadline, or the incident-response runbook was never actually tested or followed through to a completed postmortem -- resulting in prolonged exposure, an unrecovered breach, or the same root cause recurring because no lesson was captured.
